quote: I got a price there as well. I just wanted to see what is it similar? Is it different? I mean, they had a fifteen year plan.
stewart_read: Customer discloses they already spoke with a competitor and got a price with a specific plan structure. The rep acknowledges generically instead of asking which company or what the plan looked like.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately deferring competitive detail to the specialist to stay in scope — but nothing later in the call shows this was a conscious strategic choice rather than simply not asking.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one quick follow-up ("Which company was that, and what did they quote you?") — it costs 15 seconds and gives the closer real ammunition.

quote: I'm sure Sunrun took a look at it. We just need to look at the same thing.
stewart_read: The rep independently names Sunrun before the customer does, meaning the rep already has context flagged in the account — yet still doesn't ask what Sunrun proposed or whether the customer still has that quote.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may already have this logged from the lead record and see no need to re-ask — plausible, but the call gives no evidence the rep passes this context to the closer either.
coaching_implication: If the rep already knows it's Sunrun, that's exactly the moment to ask for the number so it lands in the handoff notes, not stay implicit.

quote: I think the average that I've seen is between 1,100 and 1,400 around that range per month because I do have an EV as well.
stewart_read: High usage (1,100–1,400 kWh/month) tied to EV charging is a strong system-sizing and urgency signal — a bigger system, bigger savings pitch, and a customer already primed for the electrification narrative.
coaching_implication: Rep acknowledged it ('Okay. You got an EV. That's good to know.') but never tied it back to bill savings or system sizing before pivoting into small talk about EV road trips — the anchor was available and wasn't converted into pitch language.

quote: Alright. And do you like your EV? I've been thinking of getting one, but I just I don't know.
stewart_read: Instead of using the EV/high-usage disclosure to build curiosity about the solar system size needed to offset that load, the rep pivots into a personal, off-topic EV chat for roughly a minute.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as deliberate rapport-building given the customer's warm, chatty tone — and the customer does re-engage warmly afterward, so it's not purely lost value.
coaching_implication: Rapport is fine, but the manager should note the missed bridge back to "that usage means we'd size a bigger system for you" before moving to scheduling.

quote: And do you guys do you guys offer, like, a fifteen year plan or twenty year? What was that? How that usually works?
stewart_read: Customer asks a direct financing/plan-length question post-booking. Rep admits not knowing rather than using the universal escape hatch to reframe it as specialist territory.
alternative_hypothesis: The honest scope admission ('I'm just a scheduler') is itself schema-aligned knowledge-gap handling (admit and recover with transparency) rather than a failure — it avoids fabrication.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pair the honest admission with the escape-hatch language ("that's exactly what my specialist will walk you through Friday") so the customer isn't left with an open question hanging into the handoff.

quote: Yeah. I'd like to go over that as well. So if you could just write that down in your notes.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly and directly asks the rep to document the plan-length/financing question for the specialist — a concrete, actionable handoff commitment the rep needs to honor.
coaching_implication: This is a direct customer request for a specific handoff item — the manager should confirm this note actually reaches the closer, since the call gives no verbal confirmation the rep wrote anything down.

quote: I got I got a quote from Sunrun roughly around $1.60 something a month.
stewart_read: Third instance of the customer surfacing detailed Sunrun pricing (including two-battery configuration) with no rep follow-up question — a clear repeated pattern, not a one-off.
coaching_implication: Flag this as the clearest single example to replay with the rep: the customer gave an exact monthly figure and battery count, unprompted, and the rep moved straight to Ion's own battery options without capturing the comparison detail for the closer.

quote: K. Yeah. And we have batteries as well. I know we have, we have the Tesla Powerwall batteries, and then we also have another one. I forget what it's called.
stewart_read: Rep begins describing Ion's battery product lineup from memory and visibly can't recall the second brand, exposing a knowledge gap while still in setter scope territory that belongs to the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep does correctly hand off further battery detail to the specialist immediately after ("I'll have my specialist also go into... our battery details"), which is the right recovery move even if the opening statement wobbled.
coaching_implication: The recovery redirect at the end is good; coach the rep to lead with the redirect instead of guessing at product names first, since the memory lapse costs a small amount of credibility.
